retake.waitBetweenAttempts: Next business day, subject to appointment availability

gdl.nightCurfew: No driving midnight-5 a.m. on a provisional license (under 18) unless supervised
gdl.passengerLimits: For the first 151 days (about 5 months) of a provisional license, no passengers under 18 unless accompanied by a qualified supervising driver 21+ or an immediate family member

requiredDocuments: Proof of identity and date of birth (e.g. U.S. birth certificate or passport)
Proof of lawful status / legal presence
process.realIdNotes: REAL ID requires one proof of identity/age, one proof of Social Security number, and two proofs of Maryland residency. Federal REAL ID enforcement is in effect for boarding domestic flights.
process.permitFee: $65 (new noncommercial Type I GLS learner's permit; includes conversion to a full license)
process.licenseFee: $88 (new noncommercial license age 21+, valid 8 years; under-21 terms are prorated at $11/year)
process.visionStandard: At least 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses

facts.pointSuspensionThreshold: 8-11 points in 2 years leads to suspension; 12+ points in 2 years leads to revocation
facts.moveOverRule: Move over a lane, or slow down if you cannot, for stopped emergency, tow, and service vehicles displaying warning lights
facts.schoolZoneSpeed: Reduced posted school-zone speed limit when in effect (commonly 15-25 mph)

bacAdult.display: Driving 'under the influence of alcohol per se' is defined as a blood or breath alcohol concentration of 0.08 grams per 100 mL of blood (or 210 L of breath) or more.

conditions.detail: Applies to all licensees under 21; the statute imposes a zero-tolerance 'alcohol restriction' (any alcohol in the blood), not a defined 0.02% numeric limit as in many other states.

bacUnder21.display: Maryland does not set a numeric under-21 BAC limit; instead it imposes a zero-tolerance 'alcohol restriction' prohibiting any licensee under 21 from driving with ANY alcohol in their blood, expiring at age 21.

bacCommercial.display: A person may not drive or attempt to drive a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater (results in a 1-year CDL disqualification).

conditions.detail: First-offense administrative suspension for refusing a breath/blood test is 270 days (9 months); it doubles to 2 years for a second or subsequent refusal. This is a civil MVA sanction, not a separate crime.

impliedConsentRefusal.display: Refusing a requested alcohol/drug test under Maryland's implied-consent law results in a 270-day (9-month) administrative license suspension for a first offense (2 years for a repeat refusal); the refusal itself is not a separate criminal offense.

openContainerProhibited.display: An occupant of a motor vehicle (including the driver) may not possess an open container of any alcoholic beverage, or consume one, in the passenger area of a vehicle on a highway, statewide; limited exceptions apply to for-hire vehicles (bus/taxi/limo) and motorhome living quarters for non-driver occupants.

duiFirstSuspensionDays.display: A first-offense administrative (per se) license suspension for a breath/blood test result of 0.08 or more is 180 days.

conditions.detail: 70 mph is the statutory statewide ceiling; the State Highway Administration must post this limit for it to apply on a given interstate/expressway segment (many rural interstate segments are posted lower, e.g. 65 mph).

ruralInterstateMaxMph.display: Maryland law caps any posted speed limit statewide at 70 mph; SHA posts up to this ceiling on qualifying interstates/expressways (non-limited-access highways are capped at 55 mph).

conditions.detail: Commonly posted limit on urban interstate/beltway segments near Baltimore and Washington, D.C. (e.g., I-695, MD portions of I-495).

urbanInterstateMaxMph.display: Maryland has no separate statutory 'urban interstate' limit; SHA posts case-by-case limits under its general speed-setting authority, with 55 mph commonly posted on urban beltway segments.

conditions.detail: Undivided highway in a residential district (the default residential limit).
Divided highway in a residential district.

residentialDefaultMph.display: Absent other posting, the default statutory limit is 30 mph on undivided residential-district highways and 35 mph on divided residential-district highways.

conditions.detail: Applies only within a school zone specifically designated and posted by the local authority, during school hours; the county/municipality must pay for and post the signs.

schoolZoneMph.display: Local authorities may decrease the maximum speed limit to 15 mph in a designated, posted school zone during school hours.

basicSpeedLaw.display: A person may not drive at a speed greater than reasonable and prudent under existing conditions, regardless of the posted limit.

rightTurnOnRed.display: After stopping, a driver facing a steady red signal may cautiously turn right unless a sign at that location prohibits the turn.

leftTurnOnRedFromOneWay.display: After stopping, a driver facing a steady red signal may cautiously turn left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless a sign prohibits it.

conditions.detail: Primary enforcement applies to the driver and front-seat occupants; the separate requirement that rear-seat adults (18+) buckle up is enforced only secondarily.

seatBeltEnforcement.display: Police may stop and cite a driver solely for a seat belt violation involving the driver or a front-seat occupant (primary enforcement); the rear-seat adult belt requirement is secondary-enforcement only.

conditions.detail: School bus drivers (in motion, carrying passengers) and permit/provisional holders 18+ face a total ban on any handheld phone use. General drivers may not use their hands to operate a handheld phone for any purpose other than initiating/terminating a call or powering it on/off.

handheldPhone.display: General drivers may only touch a handheld phone to start/end a call or power it on/off (all other handheld use is banned); school bus drivers in motion and 18+ learner's-permit/provisional holders face a complete handheld-phone ban.

texting.display: All drivers, regardless of age, are banned from using a handheld device to write, send, or read a text message while driving.

moveOver.display: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, service/utility vehicle, roadside-assistance vehicle, waste/recycling vehicle, or any vehicle displaying hazard lights/flares/cones, a driver must change lanes away from it if practicable, or otherwise slow to a reasonable and prudent speed; no specific mph is set in statute.

conditions.detail: Maryland's statute does not literally use a 'minutes after sunset' or 'wipers in use' trigger; it requires lighted lamps at ANY time visibility (due to darkness or weather) drops below 1,000 feet. whenWipersOn=true and minutesAfterSunset=0 are used here as the closest schema-compatible approximation of that functional rule and should not be read as the literal statutory text (see display).

headlightsRequired.display: Maryland requires lighted lamps at any time, day or night, when insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions (e.g., rain, fog) make people and vehicles not clearly discernible from 1,000 feet away — a functional visibility test, not a fixed sunset-offset or explicit wipers-in-use rule.

parkFtFromHydrant.display: A vehicle may not be parked within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

conditions.detail: This statewide 20-foot rule does not apply within Baltimore City, which sets its own local parking rules.

parkFtFromCrosswalk.display: A vehicle may not be parked within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, except in Baltimore City where local rules apply instead.

parkFtFromStopSign.display: A vehicle may not be parked within 30 feet of a flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or traffic control signal on the approach.

parkFtFromRailroad.display: A vehicle may not be parked within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

pointSystem.display: Maryland assesses points against a driving record for moving violations, which can trigger driver-improvement action, suspension, or revocation.

pointSuspension.display: Accumulating 8 points within a 2-year period triggers a notice of suspension (12+ points within 2 years triggers revocation instead).

citation.label: MVA — Driver's License Points
citation.citation: Md. Transportation Code Ann. § 16-404(a); MDOT MVA 'Driver's License Points'

permitMinAgeMonths.display: A learner's instructional permit may not be issued to anyone who has not reached the age of 15 years, 9 months (189 months).

conditions.detail: 9-month minimum applies to permit holders under 18 without a high school diploma/equivalent; the Rookie Driver program shortens this to 3 months for 18-24 year-olds with a diploma/equivalent and to 45 days for applicants 25+.

permitHoldingMonths.display: A minor must hold a learner's permit for at least 9 months before qualifying for a provisional license (shorter minimums apply to older applicants).

supervisedHoursTotal.display: A learner's permit holder must complete 60 hours of supervised practice driving before qualifying for a provisional license.

supervisedHoursNight.display: Of the 60 required supervised practice-driving hours, at least 10 must be at night.

conditions.detail: Applies to unsupervised provisional (intermediate) license holders under 18; the restriction expires the day the holder turns 18. Exceptions exist for supervised driving, employment, school activities, volunteer programs, and athletic events/training.

gdlNightCurfew.display: A provisional license holder under 18 may not drive unsupervised between midnight and 5 a.m., with exceptions for supervised driving, work, school, volunteering, or athletics; the curfew ends at age 18.

conditions.detail: In effect from the date the provisional license is issued through the 151st day after issuance; does not apply when accompanied by a supervising driver 21+ licensed 3+ years.

gdlPassengerPhase1.display: For the first 151 days after a provisional license (holder under 18) is issued, no passengers under 18 are allowed except a spouse, child, sibling, step-sibling, or a relative who lives at the same address.

minLiability.display: Maryland's minimum required liability coverage is $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 bodily injury per crash, and $15,000 property damage.

state.reason: Maryland's driver duty-to-render-aid/exchange-information and MVA crash-report statutes (Transportation §§ 20-104, 20-107) are triggered by bodily injury, death, or ANY damage to an attended vehicle or other attended property — the state does not set a minimum property-damage dollar threshold for a required crash report.

crashReportThresholdUsd.display: Not applicable: Maryland's reporting duty turns on injury/death or any attended-property damage, not a dollar threshold.
